annotations.statement: The BBC page is a news report published on 18 December 2015; the Guardian page is labelled Analysis and was published on 19 December. Their publication times are not the Council vote time.
annotations.scope: These two items and their recorded metadata only.

annotations.statement: The BBC headline foregrounds unanimity and a peace plan; the Guardian headline foregrounds a framework with gaps. This is an interpretation of the selected wording, not a finding about either publisher’s general political orientation.
annotations.scope: Selected headlines, not the full reporting or the outlets.

annotations.statement: The BBC body explicitly acknowledges disagreement over Assad’s future. Its headline emphasis should not be converted into a claim that the report omits disagreement.

The Guardian lead compresses the institutional timetable into “government”, “constitution” and “elections”. Compare that wording with paragraph 4’s distinct governance, constitutional-drafting process and election objectives before reusing it in an AI context. The source paragraph is retained separately; the analysis is not treated as its verbatim wording.
annotations.scope: A source-wording comparison, not a numerical accuracy or bias rating.
